record.title: The rig that produces and re-verifies every published privacy claim runs from two mutable :latest image tags
record.description: Both rig containers are selected by floating tags (harness/docker-compose.yml:9 electriccoinco/zcashd:latest, :34 electriccoinco/lightwalletd:latest). Nothing in the reviewed revision pins a digest, sets pull_policy or platform, or checks a repo digest (git grep '@sha256:' / 'pull_policy' / 'repoDigests' over the tracked tree: 0 hits each; '@sha256:' 0 hits across every commit), so the content that runs is chosen by whoever can re-point those Docker Hub tags, not by this repository. That content is not marginal: zcashd is the chain and the miner, and lightwalletd is the CompactTxStreamer the wallets sync against, so the pair produces every block, transaction and balance the flow runner observes, the gate's chain verification re-reads against the same endpoints (crates/probe/src/gate.rs:165, verify at :156), and the anchor timestamp is a shielded memo on that chain. The resolution point is reached by (a) any third-party workflow that uses the composite action (action.yml:85 runs harness/up.sh on the caller's runner; the action is documented as uses: memeshee/zanary@main), (b) this repo's own gate and payer jobs (.github/workflows/privacy-gate.yml:87 via uses: ./ and :239 directly) including the weekly cron (:23) on runners with no image cache, and (c) the judge-facing one command (README.md:111/114, docs/SUBMISSION.md:36). A substituted image therefore both executes on those machines and can fabricate the data a 'privacy claim' is made of, while the recorded claim carries no image, digest or container identity at all (crates/report/src/lib.rs:33-54 binds version/flow_id/flow_commit/chain/heights/findings/evidence/report_hash only), and the strongest source-visible chain control is a string equality between the node's self-reported getblockchaininfo.chain and the report's own self-asserted 'regtest' (crates/report/src/verify.rs:697) - so a drift is invisible in the evidence, the artifacts and the published page. The docs assert fixed identities that no mechanism enforces (harness/HARNESS.md:54-55 and README.md:75 name v6.20.0 / v0.5.5 next to the mutable tags). Whether the tags have in fact been re-pointed, and who can re-point them, is a registry fact this run cannot observe - hence needs_validation rather than confirmed.
record.claimed_root_cause: harness/docker-compose.yml selects both rig services by mutable tag (:9, :34) and the repository never binds the running container to a reviewed artifact: no image digest, no pull_policy, no platform pin, no repo-digest comparison anywhere in the tracked tree or history (git grep '@sha256:' / 'pull_policy' / 'repoDigests': 0 hits; the only docker inspect in the tree is harness/up.sh:116 reading .State.Running; the only docker pull is scripts/phase0-warmup.sh:31, recording no digest). The one step that could record what resolved - the bare `docker compose up -d` at harness/up.sh:60 (default pull policy `missing`, so any machine without the image cached pulls it) - records nothing, and the claim schema (crates/report/src/lib.rs:33-54) has no field for it, so the gate verdict and the published evidence are produced by an unbound third-party component.

trace.description: The chain/miner container and the indexer container are selected by floating tags (electriccoinco/zcashd:latest, electriccoinco/lightwalletd:latest); the file pins no digest, platform or pull policy, so the satisfying artifact is decided outside this repository.

`docker compose up -d` resolves those tags on whichever machine runs the harness - compose's default pull policy is `missing`, so a machine with no cached image (a fresh CI runner, a judge) pulls from the registry - and the script records nothing about what it resolved; its only identity-adjacent call (:116) reads .State.Running.

trace.scope: composite action step 'start the throwaway chain'
trace.description: A third-party workflow that consumes `uses: memeshee/zanary@main` executes this step, so the current content of both tags is pulled and run inside the caller's runner/job, which is the execution boundary the tag controller reaches.

This repository's own gate and payer jobs run the same harness/up.sh - the schedule (:23, cron 17 4 * * 1) re-runs it weekly on fresh runners - and the publish job (:110-163) renders the resulting runs to Pages, so the artifact published as the project's public privacy evidence is decided downstream of the unpinned containers.

What a claim binds: version, flow_id, flow_commit, chain ('regtest' as a self-asserted string), verified_at_height, verified_at, ttl_seconds, findings, evidence, merchant_is_simulated, report_hash - no image, digest, container or environment identity, so the container content behind a claim is unrecorded and uncheckable after the fact.

trace.scope: gate verdict (chain_verified) and its published summary
trace.description: The pass/fail verdict is re-derived from the same unbound node+indexer pair (verify_report at :156 reads the live node and indexer; the strongest chain check is the self-reported string at verify.rs:697), and the anchor it may publish (:181-206) is a shielded memo on the chain those containers produce, so the value that reaches the build result, the uploaded artifacts and the public claim index is produced by a component whose identity this repository never fixed or recorded.

evidence.description: image: electriccoinco/zcashd:latest - floating tag, no @sha256 digest, no pull_policy, no platform
image: electriccoinco/lightwalletd:latest - same for the indexer; the second service mounts nothing and adds no identity requirement
the only resolution point: bare `docker compose up -d` (the compose header documents the same command for the user)
the rig's only docker inspect call (git grep 'docker inspect': 1 hit) reads .State.Running - liveness, not image identity
run: harness/up.sh - the composite action third parties are told to use brings up the unpinned rig in their runner; its own diagnostics (:157) print {{.Image}} only, a name:tag, never a digest
run: harness/up.sh in the payer job; the gate job reaches the same step through uses: ./ at :87
weekly cron (17 4 * * 1): the gate re-probes on a fresh runner with no cached image, so a re-pointed tag is consumed by this repo's own CI with no repo change
documents `electriccoinco/zcashd:latest` (v6.20.0) - a fixed version asserted next to a mutable tag, with no mechanism enforcing either the version or the identity
'zcashd v6.20.0 regtest + lightwalletd v0.5.5, one `docker compose up -d`' - the reproducibility the README sells is not bound to the pulled artifact
'One command: harness/up.sh && scripts/demo-run.sh' - the judge-facing instruction resolves the unpinned tags on the judge's machine
'the run has a timestamp nobody had to be trusted for' - on this rig the timestamp (an anchor memo) and the run share the unpinned containers as their producer
Report struct: the published claim carries no container/image/digest identity, so drift between what produced it and what the docs name is undetectable from the evidence
the strongest source-visible chain control: equality of the node's self-reported getblockchaininfo.chain with the report's own 'regtest' string - a substituted node answers it trivially
even the repo's own warm-up pulls the same floating tag (`electriccoinco/zcashd:latest`) with a bare docker pull, recording no digest

blockers: Registry fact, not observable from source and out of bounds for this run (no registry access, no pull or inspect of the rig's images): which manifest digest docker.io/electriccoinco/zcashd:latest and docker.io/electriccoinco/lightwalletd:latest resolve to, and whether either tag has been re-pointed since the reviewed revision (introduced with the tags in e79f4e6, 2026-10-11; `git log -S':latest' -- harness/docker-compose.yml` returns only that commit).

Hosted-control fact: who holds write access to the two Docker Hub repositories (the electriccoinco org) and whether tag immutability/protection is enabled there - this decides whether a lower-trust writer of the tag exists at all, which is the precondition of the handoff.

Consumer fact: whether any run (this repo's weekly cron, a push, or a third-party workflow using the action) executed between the reviewed commit and now against container content that differs from the reviewed-era image; decidable only from the registry plus Actions logs and artifact digests that are outside this unit's reach.

No bounded local check can settle it: the decisive experiment needs a substituted node/indexer pair (a hostile lightwalletd answering CompactTxStreamer plus a node answering JSON-RPC) reachable by the probe, i.e. the rig's own images and host ports (18232/18233/9067/9068) - both explicitly out of bounds - and the approved sandbox (--network=none, no image pulls) cannot build or run them.

validation_plan.local: On a machine allowed to reach the registry (read-only; nothing pushed or published): (1) at two times at least a day apart, resolve both tags without pulling - `docker buildx imagetools inspect electriccoinco/zcashd:latest` and the same for lightwalletd:latest (fallback `docker manifest inspect --verbose <tag>`) - recording the per-platform manifest digest; (2) in a disposable checkout of the reviewed commit run `harness/up.sh` once and immediately capture `docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' zanary-zcashd` and the same for zanary-lwd; a digest that changes between the two observations while harness/docker-compose.yml is unchanged is the missing drift observation, and if the machine that produced the recorded/golden evidence still holds those images, `docker image inspect --format '{{.RepoDigests}}'` it and compare (the recorded evidence itself cannot supply the baseline - that is the finding). A check needing no registry at all: `docker compose -f harness/docker-compose.yml config --images` shows the resolved references carry no @sha256.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, no probing: on the CI runner used by the privacy-gate jobs (and for one third-party caller of the action), add an always-run step alongside the existing rig-diagnostics step (action.yml:149-170) printing `docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}} {{index .RepoDigests 0}}' zanary-zcashd zanary-lwd` into the job summary, and read it across two runs a week apart; if the digests differ on an unchanged harness/docker-compose.yml, the tag drifted under a claim that is still published. Closure (repo-side, non-destructive): pin both services to the observed digests, have harness/up.sh compare the running containers' RepoDigests against the pins before the flow runs, and record the observed digest in the claim/summary so a claim names the container content that produced it.
